messages:
maria: hey team, maria here — first day on runtime. Trying to get a dev build working and hitting a runtime load error when running the tests. any quick onboarding checklist?

maria: host: Fedora 36 (WSL2 VM), NVIDIA driver 515.x installed via distro, cuda toolkit 11.8 in /opt/cuda-11.8. build fails at test-run with: 
```
./bin/redwood-infer: error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

maria: ldconfig shows libcuda.so.1 at /usr/lib64/nvidia, but the binary still complains.

jay: welcome! :wave: quick things — are you running in a container or on host? Also check that LD_LIBRARY_PATH isn't being clobbered by the test harness.

maria: running tests on host first. LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes /usr/lib64/nvidia and /opt/cuda-11.8/lib64.

infra-bot: Note: some Fedora packages install libcuda under /usr/lib64/nvidia/libcuda.so.1 and require an extra symlink at /usr/lib/libcuda.so.1 for older loaders. See infra ticket #4821.

kevin: if the loader still can't find it, run `ldd ./bin/redwood-infer` to see where it's looking. Also `strace -e openat ./bin/redwood-infer` can show the search path.

maria: ldd shows libcuda.so.1 => not found. `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` lists it under /usr/lib64/nvidia/libcuda.so.1.

tanvi: if ldconfig knows it but the binary doesn't, maybe the test binary was built with RPATH set to something else. Check `readelf -d ./bin/redwood-infer | grep RPATH`

maria: readelf shows RUNPATH set to $ORIGIN/../lib. Hmm. The runtime expects bundled libs in build/lib which we didn't install.

jay: aha — our dev docs mention two ways: either install NVIDIA driver libs system-wide or set `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$PWD/build/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before running tests. The CI uses the first approach.

maria: setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH to include build/lib made the binary start but then I hit CUDA driver API mismatches: "cuDeviceGet returned 35".

kevin: code 35 is CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_IMAGE or similar — usually driver/runtime mismatch. Which libcuda is being used (driver) vs which toolkit lib was linked? `nvcc --version` and `nvidia-smi` outputs?

maria: nvcc reports 11.8, nvidia-smi shows driver 515.76. But the toolkit in build/lib is from a local copy of 11.2 leftover from another project (my bad).

tanvi: yep that'll do it. We should avoid mixing toolkit libs across versions. Clean the build and ensure your CMake sets CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR to /opt/cuda-11.8. Also delete build cache: `rm -rf build && cmake -S . -B build -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/opt/cuda-11.8`

maria: doing that now. also wondering: who to ping for permissions to use our shared dev gpunode? I tried SSH and /dev/nvidia* shows permission denied.

infra-bot: dev-gpunode access is granted by infra@redwood. Open a ticket with your username and we'll add you to the gpu-users group. TL;DR: you need group write on /dev/nvidiactl.

jay: if you need quick runs, use `docker run --gpus all` on your machine only if nvidia-container-runtime is installed. On Fedora it's sometimes not packaged by distro. Ask infra for the container runtime and secure group setup.

maria: clean build with correct toolkit root fixed the driver API error. Tests now spawn but a few failed kernel JITs complaining about architecture mismatch: "ptxas: error: ptxas fatal: Ptx assembly is incompatible with --gpu-name sm_80"

kevin: what's your target arch setting? We use CMake variable CUDA_ARCHS in our repo. Check `grep -R "CUDA_ARCHS" -n .` or `cmake -LA -B build | grep CUDA`

maria: cmake cache had CUDA_ARCHS=sm_80;sm_86;sm_90 from my old config. My physical GPU is an RTX 3080 (sm_86) so sm_80 caused the ptx mismatch for a generated PTX variant.

tanvi: our build system auto-generates cubin/ptx for configured archs. For local dev, keep it minimal: `-DCUDA_ARCHS=86` or set `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` depending on the CMake version.

maria: changed to 86 and rebuilt. kernels pass. Thanks! I pushed a tiny onboarding PR that adds a short checklist: toolkit root, LD_LIBRARY_PATH note, and who to ask for gpunode access.

jay: awesome — can you link the PR here once ready? we'll review quickly.

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/512 (draft) — includes exact cmake commands and the docker fallback.

docbot: Heads-up: please add an entry under docs/dev-setup.md so future new hires see the gpunode access steps.

maria: will do. thanks everyone for the quick help, super grateful! :raised_hands:
